# phare_integration_ntfy (Resource)

Manages an ntfy integration in Phare, publishing alerts to an ntfy topic. Integrations belong to the organization and are used by alert rules to send notifications. [See docs](https://docs.phare.io/integrations/ntfy).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "phare_integration_ntfy" "public" {
  name = "Ops notifications"

  settings = {
    hostname = "ntfy.sh"
    topic    = "phare-alerts-3f9c2a"
  }
}

variable "ntfy_access_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "phare_integration_ntfy" "self_hosted" {
  name = "Self-hosted ntfy"

  settings = {
    hostname     = "ntfy.example.com"
    topic        = "phare-alerts"
    access_token = var.ntfy_access_token
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Integration name, must be unique across all the integrations of the organization
- `settings` (Attributes) Settings of the ntfy integration (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Date of creation
- `id` (Number) Integration ID
- `paused` (Boolean) Whether the integration is paused, integrations can only be paused from the control panel
- `updated_at` (String) Date of last update

<a id="nestedatt--settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `settings`

Required:

- `hostname` (String) Hostname of the ntfy server, without scheme (e.g. `ntfy.sh`)
- `topic` (String) ntfy topic receiving the alerts (1-255 characters)

Optional:

- `access_token` (String, Sensitive) ntfy access token used for authenticated topics (32 characters starting with `tk_`). The API never returns this value, it is kept from the Terraform state and changes made outside of Terraform are not detected.
